The authors did not repeat training over multiple seeds, used one 4B model with LoRA and fixed low-compute budgets, and did not test transfer to natural-language benchmarks. They explicitly frame results as empirical observations under interacting composition, size, token and optimization limits, rather than universal scaling laws.

repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2604.18381.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Hand-designed procedural templates generate counting, graph and spatial problems with deterministic ground truth. Ten models calibrate difficulty; GPT-4o normalizes graph outputs and is a spatial parsing fallback.
  • Qwen3-4B LoRA/GRPO uses easy or mixed subsets of 100, 200 or 500 examples under fixed budgets. Counting rewards include format and verbosity components in addition to correctness.
  • Difficulty dimensions co-vary, and graph extraction failures/token cutoffs constrain observed performance. The study does not repeat multiple seeds or test natural-language benchmark transfer.
  • Counting prose reports 50.0/50.5/40.0 solving accuracy for Mixed100/200/500; Table 2 separately labels 44.2/43.4/35.5 as mean test accuracy. These presentations are preserved without inventing a reconciliation or universal fivefold data-efficiency result.

repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2607.27189.result

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • The v2 paper reports 160 private tasks in ten synthetic company worlds and a separate ten-task public dev world. U.S. GAAP close-cycle tasks omit tax, audit, consolidation, multi-entity/multi-currency work and external reporting.
  • Forty-two accounting experts specify/review worlds and author/solve tasks/rubrics; most world files are synthetically populated under expert review. Independent experts re-solve twenty tasks as a QC check.
  • DeepSeek-v4-Flash with a GEPA-optimized prompt grades final answers against binary outcome-based criteria. Judge selection/calibration uses 1,687 majority-vote labels from 120 trajectories of three solvers and three human raters; 97.1% agreement is that sample result, not an independently held-out accuracy guarantee.
  • Eight runs are planned per task. Mean Criteria@3 uses three runs selected lexicographically by task ID; Pass@8 is any complete success and Pass^8 requires all eight. Model-caused failures are zero; infrastructure failures are excluded, leaving 156-160 tasks per paired comparison.
  • Difficulty selection retains hard worlds under three frontier filtering models, and clarification/human-in-the-loop tasks are excluded.
  • The authors report a self-preference stress test with the judge also solving the benchmark and interpret its 37.1% middle/lower score as no material self-preference. That limited author test does not independently rule out judge bias.
  • This repair uses the v2 paper count only. A prior reference to a separate 100-task leaderboard/card conflict is not reasserted: those distinct artifacts were not read or reconciled here. No private corpus, score reproduction, independent bias audit or source-contribution inference is claimed.

repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2610.01306.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Evaluation covers 50 healthcare and 80 finance tasks; all 50 healthcare and 50 finance tasks are public. Public-finance file/rubric descriptive statistics refer to the 50 released finance tasks.
  • The offline Harbor/OpenHands protocol uses a Claude Opus 4.8-based agentic judge that inspects files, rendered outputs and trajectories; this is model grading rather than fresh human grading of every attempt.
  • Errored attempts are excluded from each task mean, so scored attempt counts can differ. Tasks are weighted equally within each domain; relaxed rubric thresholds can miss a decisive criterion.
  • Healthcare professional times are creator range estimates, averaged at midpoints with more-than-40 capped at 40. The finance mean is separately reported on its dataset card; the healthcare estimation convention is not asserted for finance.
  • Section 5.3 cost covers agent/condenser model calls and excludes the judge. It is not interpreted as an all-in service price or observed labor saving.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

PLE describes 85 tasks: 44 engineer-authored and 41 human/agent-coauthored. Coauthored tasks use expert briefs, a Claude Opus 5 Creator–Solver loop and final engineer validation. Expert tasks receive LLM-judged weighted rubric scores; most coauthored tasks combine constraint fraction with a hard-gated objective term, with four bespoke grading exceptions.

repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2610.30537.method

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Forty-four tasks are authored end to end by Mercor-recruited practising engineers. Forty-one coauthored tasks use engineer briefs, Claude Opus 5 Creator/Claude Code and Solver/Hermes, followed by expert validation and difficulty intensification.
  • Expert tasks use weighted binary rubrics judged by Claude Opus 5.5. Thirty-seven coauthored tasks use constraint/objective scoring, while four site/MEP tasks retain bespoke graders; selected narrative items are also model-judged.
  • The hybrid score is s=0.4p+0.6G Oprime. Hard gate G removes objective credit but does not generally zero the constraint-fraction term; the four bespoke task graders have separately stated gate behavior.
  • Fourteen models are evaluated under restricted harness coverage, rather than a complete 14-by-7 Cartesian crossing; Grok Build is model-specific beyond the seven named common harnesses. Results must identify the model and harness.
  • Scores average three runs per task. Single-task variance and model-judge regrading/self-preference are reported; regrading by other models is not independent human validation of engineering ground truth.
  • The paper plans to release 29 of 85 tasks. This repair does not verify present release availability or independently audit codes, physics, source rights or reference optima; mean benchmark score is not deployment certification.
